content.title: Full list of Oscar ties as The Singers and Two People Exchanging Saliva win
content.text: The Academy Awards handed the Oscar for Best Live-Action Short Film to two nominees on Sunday, marking only the seventh time the award has been shared in the academy's history. "The Singers" and "Two People Exchanging Saliva" took the award in a stunning move that host Conan O'Brien said "ruined 22 million Oscar betting pools." A tie has happened only six other times, with the first happening in 1932 and the most recent tie occurring in 1995. The categories and films that saw a tie are as follows: Best Actor in 1932 – Fredric March for Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde and Wallace Beery for The ChampBest Documentary Short Subject in 1950 – A Chance to Live and So Much for So LittleBest Actress in 1969 – Katharine Hepburn for The Lion in Winter and Barbra Streisand for Funny GirlBest Documentary (Feature) in 1986 - Artie Shaw: Time is All You've Got and Down and Out in AmericaBest Live Action Short Film in 1995 – Trevor and Franz Kafka’s It’s a Wonderful LifeBest Sound Editing in 2013 – Skyfall and Zero Dark ThirtyWhen asked about the tie, The Singers producer Jack Piatt said it was "incredible." “We’ve got to know all the other filmmakers in our category, so that was really special," Piatt said, according to IndieWire. "I wish there could be a five-way tie, to be honest with you.”How Does An Oscars Tie Happen?The Academy Awards are handed out based on votes, meaning a tie can be declared if two nominees receive the same votes - making it just highly unlikely that a tie can happen. In the case of March and Beery, the Academy noted on its website that the actors did not have a "true" tie, as March had one more vote than Beery, but rules at the time stated that if nominees were within three votes of the winner, they would also receive the award. The rules have been changed since that first tie, requiring an exact match in votes to qualify as a tie. As such, even though there have been seven overall ties at the Oscars now, only six count as true ties. Update 3/15/26, 10:11 p.m. ET: This article has been updated with additional information.
